'''Mok''' (/mɔ̀k/ 'mountain people'<ref name="Tannumsaeng2020"/>), also known as '''Amok''',<ref>OLAC Resources in and about the Mok Language, www.language-archives.org/language.php/mqt.</ref> Hsen-Hsum, and Muak, is an [[Angkuic languages|Angkuic]] language or dialect cluster spoken in [[Shan State]], [[Myanmar]]<ref name="Hall2018"/>

Seven speakers in [[Lampang province]], Thailand, were reported by [[Stephen Wurm|Wurm]] & Hattori (1981).

==Varieties==
Hall & Devereux (2018) report that five [[Variety (linguistics)|varieties]] of Mok are spoken in [[Shan State]], [[Myanmar]], providing the following comparative vocabulary table.<ref name="Hall2018">Hall, Elizabeth and Shane Devereux (2018). ''Preliminary Mok Phonology and Implications for Angkuic Sound Change.'' Paper presented at the 28th Annual Meeting of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society, held May 17–19, 2018 in Kaohsiung, Taiwan.</ref> These varieties have some lexical similarity (the lowest being 88%) with each other, but very low lexical similarity with the other Angkuic languages.<ref name=":0">Phakawee Tannumsaeng (2020). ''A Preliminary Grammar of Mok, Hwe Koi Variety, Chiang Rai, With Special Focus on the Anaphoric Use of tɤ́ʔ''. Payap University.</ref>

Owen (2018) names these varieties Hwe Law, Chieng Kham, Pha Lam, Punglong, and Hwe Koi.<ref>Owen, Robert Wyn. 2018. ''Initial findings from Mok KIQ and DMT''. Unpublished manuscript.</ref>

A Mok dialect of Shan State has been documented by Shintani (2019).<ref>Shintani, Tadahiko. 2019. ''The Sen Tsum (I-Mok) language''. Linguistic survey of Tay cultural area (LSTCA) no. 121. Tokyo: Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa (ILCAA).</ref>

== Geographic distribution ==
Tannumsaeng (2020)<ref name=":0" /> describes three locations for Mok: between [[Mong Khet Township|Mong Khet]] and [[Mong Yang Township|Mong Yang]] and south of [[Kengtung]] in [[Myanmar]], and on the Thai-Burmese border in [[Chiang Rai Province]], [[Thailand]]. The main Mok-speaking areas in Shan State include an area just to the south of [[Kengtung]], and another area situated between Mong Khet and Mong Yang.<ref name="Tannumsaeng2020">Tannumsaeng, Phakawee. 2020. ''[https://ic.payap.ac.th/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/Opel-Thesis.pdf A Preliminary Grammar of Mok, Hwe Koi Variety, Chiang Rai, with Special Focus on The Anaphoric Uses of tɤ́ʔ]''. M.A. dissertation. Chiang Mai: Payap University.</ref>

== Phonology ==
Tannumsaeng (2020),<ref name=":0" /> citing Hall & Devereux (2018), provides the following [[phonology]] for Mok.

The [[consonant]]s are /pʰ p m f w tʰ t n s l r c ɲ j kʰ k ŋ ʔ h/, with reduced /m̩ n̩ ɲ̩ ŋ̍ pə tə kə sə/. /f/ and /r/ only appear in certain varieties. The [[vowel]]s are /i e ɛ u ɯ o ɤ ɔ a/, with the [[diphthong]]s /ia ɯa ua/. Mok has two [[Tone (linguistics)|tones]], one low and one high.
